headline: 4 die of dengue in 24 hours, 1,851 hospitalised
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reported four new dengue deaths and 1,851 hospitalizations in the last 24 hours. This brings the total dengue death toll this year to 352.
details: At least four dengue patients have died and 1,851 others were admitted to hospitals in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00 AM today. This marks a significant daily increase in cases and fatalities.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), two of the reported deaths occurred within the Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) area, one in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC), and another in the Mymensingh division.
With these latest figures, the total number of dengue deaths recorded this year has climbed to 352. The total number of dengue cases reported nationwide has reached 114,251.

Currently, there are 6,033 dengue patients undergoing treatment at various hospitals across the country. Health authorities continue to urge the public to take preventative measures against mosquito bites.

headline: 1,201 dead as measles outbreak toll tops 1,200 in Bangladesh
summary: Five more people died in 24 hours, with Dhaka Division recording the highest number of fatalities according to the DGHS.
details: Five more people with symptoms of measles have died across Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The total number of deaths among people with measles symptoms has reached 1,201 this year, including 1,097 suspected cases and 104 confirmed cases.
Dhaka Division has been the hardest hit, recording 493 deaths, followed by Chattogram with 101, Rajshahi 93, and Mymensingh 84.
In the last 24 hours alone, 1,307 people with measles symptoms sought treatment at hospitals nationwide, with 1,179 being admitted.
The DGHS reported that 214,551 people have shown measles symptoms, and 23,157 of these cases have been confirmed as measles.
Total hospital admissions have reached 190,663, with 183,042 patients having recovered and returned home.
The DGHS has been tracking these infections and deaths since March 15. However, the actual number of confirmed cases remains undetermined as not all patients are tested.
caption:
Over 1,200 people have died in Bangladesh's measles outbreak this year. Five more fatalities were reported in just 24 hours.

Five more people with symptoms of measles have died across Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

The total number of deaths among people with measles symptoms has reached 1,201 this year, including 1,097 suspected cases and 104 confirmed cases.

Dhaka Division has been the hardest hit, recording 493 deaths, followed by Chattogram with 101, Rajshahi 93, and Mymensingh 84.

In the last 24 hours alone, 1,307 people with measles symptoms sought treatment at hospitals nationwide, with 1,179 being admitted.

The DGHS reported that 214,551 people have shown measles symptoms, and 23,157 of these cases have been confirmed as measles.

Total hospital admissions have reached 190,663, with 183,042 patients having recovered and returned home.

The DGHS has been tracking these infections and deaths since March 15. However, the actual number of confirmed cases remains undetermined as not all patients are tested.
